\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{عارضی} (ārzī)}{عارضی (ārzī)}]{\ur{عارضی} (ārzī) — temporary}

\label{lesson:UR-C545-arzi}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for a series, then the Urdu for order (a set sequence).
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{عارضی}}
\textbf{\ur{عارضی}} — \emph{ārzī} — \textquotedblleft{}temporary\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{اگر} \ur{یہ} \ur{نوکری} \ur{عارضی} \ur{ہے} \ur{تو} \ur{میں} \ur{نہیں} \ur{لوں} \ur{گا۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{agar yih naukrī ārzī hai to maiṅ nahīṅ lūṅ gā.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
If this job is temporary, I won't take it.
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{عارضی}} (\emph{ārzī}) is usually traced, through Persian, to Arabic \emph{ʿāriḍī}, \textquotedblleft{}passing, accidental\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for saying what happens if.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ārzī}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ārzī}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{agar yih naukrī ārzī hai to maiṅ nahīṅ lūṅ gā.} — If this job is temporary, I won't take it.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Urdu for a series, then the Urdu for order (a set sequence), then say \emph{ārzī} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ur{عارضی} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}Temporary\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{مستقل} (mustaqil)}{مستقل (mustaqil)}]{\ur{مستقل} (mustaqil) — permanent; steady}

\label{lesson:UR-C545-mustaqil}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for order (a set sequence), then the Urdu for temporary.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{مستقل}}
\textbf{\ur{مستقل}} — \emph{mustaqil} — \textquotedblleft{}permanent; steady\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{اگر} \ur{نوکری} \ur{مستقل} \ur{ہوئی} \ur{تو} \ur{ہم} \ur{نیا} \ur{گھر} \ur{لیں} \ur{گے۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{agar naukrī mustaqil huī to ham nayā ghar leṅ ge.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
If the job becomes permanent, we'll get a new house.
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{مستقل}} (\emph{mustaqil}) is usually traced, through Persian, to Arabic \emph{mustaqill}, \textquotedblleft{}standing on its own, independent\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for saying what happens if.

  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Urdu for order (a set sequence), then the Urdu for temporary, then say \emph{mustaqil} again

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{حتمی} (hatmī)}{حتمی (hatmī)}]{\ur{حتمی} (hatmī) — final; definite}

\label{lesson:UR-C545-hatmi}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for temporary, then the Urdu for permanent.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{حتمی}}
\textbf{\ur{حتمی}} — \emph{hatmī} — \textquotedblleft{}final; definite\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{اگر} \ur{یہ} \ur{تاریخ} \ur{حتمی} \ur{ہے} \ur{تو} \ur{میں} \ur{ٹکٹ} \ur{خریدوں} \ur{گا۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{agar yih tārīkh hatmī hai to maiṅ ṭikaṭ kharīdūṅ gā.}

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{حتمی}} (\emph{hatmī}) is usually traced, through Persian, to Arabic \emph{ḥatmī}, \textquotedblleft{}decisive\textquotedblright{}, built on \emph{ḥatm}, \textquotedblleft{}deciding finally\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{مرحلہ} (marhalā)}{مرحلہ (marhalā)}]{\ur{مرحلہ} (marhalā) — a stage (of a process)}

\label{lesson:UR-C545-marhala}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for permanent, then the Urdu for final.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{مرحلہ}}
\textbf{\ur{مرحلہ}} — \emph{marhalā} — \textquotedblleft{}a stage (of a process)\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{اگر} \ur{ہم} \ur{نے} \ur{پہلا} \ur{مرحلہ} \ur{جیتا} \ur{تو} \ur{آگے} \ur{جائیں} \ur{گے۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{agar ham ne pehlā marhalā jītā to āge jāeṅ ge.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
If we win the first stage, we'll go through.
\end{quote}

Masculine.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{مرحلہ}} (\emph{marhalā}) is usually traced, through Persian, to Arabic \emph{marḥala}, \textquotedblleft{}a day's journey, a stage\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for saying what happens if.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}

\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{marhalā}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{marhalā}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{agar ham ne pehlā marhalā jītā to āge jāeṅ ge.} — If we win the first stage, we'll go through.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Urdu for permanent, then the Urdu for final, then say \emph{marhalā} again
\end{itemize}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{پائیدار} (pāedār)}{پائیدار (pāedār)}]{\ur{پائیدار} (pāedār) — durable; hard-wearing}

\label{lesson:UR-C545-paedar}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for final, then the Urdu for a stage.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{پائیدار}}
\textbf{\ur{پائیدار}} — \emph{pāedār} — \textquotedblleft{}durable; hard-wearing\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{اگر} \ur{جوتا} \ur{پائیدار} \ur{ہوتا} \ur{تو} \ur{ابھی} \ur{تک} \ur{چلتا۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{agar jūtā pāedār hotā to abhī tak chaltā.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
If the shoe were well made, it would still be going.
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{پائیدار}} (\emph{pāedār}) is usually traced to Persian \emph{pāydār}, \textquotedblleft{}lasting, firm\textquotedblright{}, built from \emph{pāy}, \textquotedblleft{}a foot\textquotedblright{}, and \emph{-dār}, \textquotedblleft{}holding\textquotedblright{}: keeping its footing.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for saying what happens if.
\end{grammarlens}

\raggedright

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{pāedār}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{agar jūtā pāedār hotā to abhī tak chaltā.} — If the shoe were well made, it would still be going.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Urdu for final, then the Urdu for a stage, then say \emph{pāedār} again
\end{itemize}
